definitions.gloss: to go through, to use as an intermediary
definitions.explanation: To use something or someone as a means, channel, or intermediary. Almost always appears in the pattern 〜を{介|かい}して (through ~, via ~).
To be bothered by or concerned about something. Used in the negative pattern {意|い}に{介|かい}さない (not to care, not to be bothered).

examples.japanese: インターネットを{介|かい}して{情報|じょうほう}を{得|え}る。
{通訳|つうやく}を{介|かい}して{会話|かいわ}した。
{友人|ゆうじん}を{介|かい}して{紹介|しょうかい}してもらった。
examples.english: I was introduced through a friend.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{批判|ひはん}を{意|い}に{介|かい}さない。
{周囲|しゅうい}の{反対|はんたい}を{意|い}に{介|かい}さず、{自分|じぶん}の{道|みち}を{進|すす}んだ。
examples.english: Without caring about the opposition around him, he pursued his own path.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{失敗|しっぱい}をまったく{意|い}に{介|かい}していないようだった。
examples.english: She didn't seem to care about the failure at all.

notes:
This verb almost always appears in fixed patterns rather than being used freely.

KEY PATTERNS:
・〜を{介|かい}して (through ~, via ~) — sense 1
・〜を{介|かい}する (to go through ~) — sense 1
・{意|い}に{介|かい}さない (not to care about, not to be bothered by) — sense 2

Sense 1 is formal and commonly appears in written language, news, and business contexts. {通|つう}じて (through) is a more casual alternative.

Sense 2 almost exclusively appears in the set phrase {意|い}に{介|かい}さない / {意|い}に{介|かい}する. The affirmative {意|い}に{介|かい}する is rare; the negative form is far more common.
